A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RESM study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison. v4 adds acknowledgments, references, and a conference checklist.

before.justification: v3 reports original DPO and model-merging experiments on Llama3 and Mistral, including benchmark results, ablations, and appendix robustness analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments, including the static and continual optimization results in Tables 3–7 and 10–11.

M1.justification: RESM's outlier weighting, sparsity-adaptive rank selection, orthogonalization, and merging procedure remain unchanged in Equations 4–9 and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten preference datasets, five annotation groups, and helpfulness, honesty, and harmlessness evaluation tasks. Static and continual DPO scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same data-mixture and merging comparators, including TSVM+Wanda and TSVM+Owl in Table 5. DAM is newly mentioned in Appendix B.2 but is not added to the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: The backbones, training settings, static and continual evaluation procedures, and Table 9 sample counts, judge models, and metrics are unchanged. The checklist supplies no new experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The model-count and effective-rank analyses in Figure 2, component ablations in Tables 6–7, and seed and sparsity sensitivity analyses in Figures 5–6 are retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: The same seed-sensitivity plots and point-estimate tables remain. Checklist item 7 asserts adequate statistical reporting but adds no run counts, uncertainty estimates, significance tests, or estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and experimental plots are unchanged. For example, RESM's static normalized gains remain 14.97% on Llama3 and 3.36% on Mistral; continual gains remain 14.56% and 2.83%, respectively.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1–15, Appendix A conflict-probability derivation, and Table 8 theoretical comparison are unchanged apart from typesetting.

C1.justification: The central claims about the first systematic benchmark, 3H trade-offs, RESM's contribution, and gains over data mixture and existing merging methods retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and Appendix D limitations concerning helpfulness and inter- versus intra-dimension conflicts remain. The added closing sentence calls generically for broader trustworthy applications without establishing a new substantive limitation or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: v4 removes the abstract's model-release statement and 3H_Merging hyperlink. Appendix C.1 still promises future release, while the new checklist asserts open access without replacement access instructions. Hyperparameters, software, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged; actual online availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v4 adds fourteen references, including SafeLawBench, text detoxification, and broader trustworthiness and diffusion-model work. Appendix B.2 also adds DAM to its discussion. These are limited extensions of the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized wording and terminology edits, updates correspondence and conference text, and adds acknowledgments and a largely templated NeurIPS checklist. The research narrative and organization of Appendices A–D remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is revised with an explicit model-merging label and adjusted caption. Added sections and formatting changes cause page reflow, while Figures 2–6 and the table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Editorial refinements and additional citations provide modest benefits, but v4 removes the model-access link without replacing it and introduces inconsistent documentation. Checklist item 12 states that no existing assets are used, despite the datasets and pretrained backbones specified in Section 5.1. Together with the unresolved release statements, this weakens access clarity and internal consistency. The scientific method and evidence remain unchanged, so the deterioration is limited.
